questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: A humanoid robot that creates art and its creators
Why Hollywood films about dangerous robots are so popular
How modern artists use computers to paint their pictures
The life of a famous 19th-century female mathematician
questions.why: They talk about Ai-Da, a robot artist, and the inventors behind her.

questions.q: How does Ai-Da make her drawings?
options: She copies pictures that she finds on the internet
A human artist holds and guides her robotic hand
She paints only from memory, without looking at anything
She uses a camera in her eye and a pencil in a robotic arm
questions.why: She uses a robotic arm and a pencil to draw what she sees with a camera in her eye.

questions.q: Where were Ai-Da's robotic arms built?
options: In Cornwall
In Leeds
At Oxford University
In London
questions.why: Engineers in Leeds built her robotic arms using AI systems from Oxford University.

questions.q: How did Karl Bos's feelings about Ai-Da change?
options: He liked her at first but then found her frightening
He was bored by her from the start
She looked scary at first but seemed cute once she moved
He thought she looked too much like a real person
questions.why: He says she looks scary at first glance, but when she moves and expresses she becomes very cute.

questions.q: According to Marcus Hold, what makes the robots seem human?
options: The way they move and behave
Their realistic skin
Their ability to speak many languages
Their intelligence
questions.why: He says a big part of their appeal and human nature is in the way they behave and move.

questions.q: What was Aidan Meller's job before managing the Ai-Da project?
options: Robotics engineer
BBC presenter
Art gallery owner
University researcher
questions.why: Neil introduces him as a former art gallery owner.

questions.q: What does Aidan Meller say the team was still working on?
options: Giving Ai-Da a voice so she could talk to visitors
Finding a museum for her show
Making her skin look real
Getting her arm to draw well
questions.why: He says some people were working on her arm, getting her to do a compelling drawing.

questions.q: What does Neil suggest when he says a robot could be 'the next Picasso'?
options: Robots will soon replace all human artists and designers
It is nicer to imagine robots making art than taking control
Picasso's famous paintings were really made by machines
Ai-Da has been trained to copy Picasso's style exactly
questions.why: He says it's nice to think a robot could be the next Picasso 'instead of an out-of-control sci-fi policeman'.
